project.name: Elysium
project.summary: A luxury jewellery e-commerce storefront built with Next.js. Customers browse engagement rings and fine jewellery, configure ring options, and check out with Stripe. Staff manage orders, inventory and bespoke enquiries through an admin dashboard. Product content comes from Sanity CMS and a local catalogue, with data kept in PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Storefront
nodes.summary: The customer-facing website: homepage, product pages, collection browsing, shopping cart, checkout and account screens.

nodes.label: Pages
nodes.summary: Each screen a customer can visit: home, shop, collections, product detail, cart, checkout, about, contact, FAQs and policies.

nodes.label: Page sections
nodes.summary: Reusable building blocks that make up the homepage and landing pages: hero banners, product carousels, testimonials, trust badges and category showcases.

nodes.label: Product experience
nodes.summary: Everything on a product page: photo gallery, zoom, configuration options (metal, size, stone), sticky price summary, reviews, recently viewed, and share-a-build.

nodes.label: Browsing & filters
nodes.summary: Lets customers narrow products by shape, metal, price and other attributes using a filter drawer and chips.

nodes.label: Bespoke enquiry
nodes.summary: A step-by-step wizard where customers describe a custom ring they'd like made, including file uploads and budget.

nodes.label: Cart & wishlist
nodes.summary: The slide-out cart drawer, mini cart icon and wishlist heart button that let customers save and buy items.

nodes.label: Shared UI kit
nodes.summary: Common building blocks used across every screen: header, buttons, product cards, breadcrumbs, search bar, image loader, modals, accessibility helpers and loading spinners.

nodes.label: Concierge chat
nodes.summary: A floating chat widget that offers personal shopping assistance to visitors.

nodes.label: Privé collection
nodes.summary: An invitation-only or coming-soon collection page with a waitlist sign-up modal.

nodes.label: Fine jewellery
nodes.summary: Browsing and hero sections for the fine-jewellery category: earrings, necklaces, bracelets.

nodes.label: Admin dashboard
nodes.summary: A staff-only area for managing orders, inventory levels, bespoke enquiries, and viewing sales statistics.

nodes.label: TMC review tool
nodes.summary: An internal tool for reviewing and selecting rings from TMC (The Master Craftsman) supplier catalogue for inclusion in the Elysium storefront.

nodes.label: Server
nodes.summary: The Next.js API routes that power everything behind the screens: user accounts, shopping cart, checkout, orders, inventory, wishlists, bespoke enquiries and admin operations.

nodes.label: Sign-in
nodes.summary: Handles customer registration, email/password login and Google sign-in so people can track orders and save wishlists.

nodes.label: Shopping requests
nodes.summary: Requests for the cart, checkout, orders, products, inventory, wishlists, recently-viewed tracking and waitlist sign-ups.

nodes.label: Admin requests
nodes.summary: Staff-only requests for the dashboard: sales stats, order management, inventory updates and bespoke enquiry handling.

nodes.label: Stripe alerts
nodes.summary: Stripe calls this when a payment succeeds, fails or is refunded, so the order status updates automatically.

nodes.label: Supplier integrations
nodes.summary: Requests that talk to the Nivoda diamond marketplace and TMC supplier catalogue.

nodes.label: Shared logic
nodes.summary: Business logic and helpers used by both screens and the server: database queries, authentication checks, payment processing, email sending, product data and validation.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.summary: The Prisma client setup and direct database queries for reading and writing orders, cart items, inventory and customer data.

nodes.label: Business services
nodes.summary: The core business logic: managing the cart, processing orders, tracking inventory, handling bespoke leads, sending emails, recording analytics and admin authentication.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.summary: NextAuth.js configuration for customer sign-in (email/password and Google) and admin access checks.

nodes.label: Payments
nodes.summary: Stripe integration for taking card payments at checkout and processing webhook events.

nodes.label: Content (Sanity)
nodes.summary: Fetches product descriptions, images and editorial content from the Sanity headless CMS.

nodes.label: Product catalogue
nodes.summary: Product definitions, pricing, filtering logic, image resolution and the local catalogue data that powers the shop when Sanity isn't involved.

nodes.label: Validation
nodes.summary: Input validation rules for checkout forms, bespoke enquiries and other user-submitted data.

nodes.label: App state
nodes.summary: Zustand store that keeps the cart and other session data in sync across screens.

nodes.label: Screen helpers
nodes.summary: React hooks that add scroll animations, parallax effects, keyboard navigation, performance monitoring and wishlist/recently-viewed tracking to the screens.

nodes.label: Data & schema
nodes.summary: The database schema (Prisma), Sanity CMS content schemas, and TypeScript type definitions that describe products, orders and other business objects.

nodes.label: Build & import scripts
nodes.summary: One-off and recurring scripts: importing products from the TMC supplier, building image manifests, seeding the database, auditing data, and setting up third-party services.

nodes.label: Tests
nodes.summary: Playwright browser tests and integration test support for the storefront.

nodes.label: Configuration
nodes.summary: Build and deploy settings: Next.js config, Tailwind theme, TypeScript, ESLint, PostCSS, Playwright and Vercel deployment.

nodes.label: Stripe
nodes.summary: Handles card payments and sends alerts when payments succeed or fail.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.summary: The database where all customer accounts, orders, cart items, inventory and enquiries are stored.

nodes.label: Sanity CMS
nodes.summary: A headless content management system that stores product descriptions, images and editorial content.

nodes.label: Nivoda
nodes.summary: A diamond marketplace that supplies loose stones and pricing data.

nodes.label: Resend
nodes.summary: Sends transactional emails: order confirmations, bespoke enquiry notifications and admin alerts.

edges.label: Payment alerts
edges.description: Stripe sends a message when a payment succeeds, fails or is disputed.

edges.label: Reads/writes
edges.description: Every server request reads or writes customer, order and inventory records.

edges.label: Fetches content
edges.description: Pulls product descriptions and editorial content from the CMS.

edges.label: Sends emails
edges.description: Sends order confirmations, enquiry alerts and admin notifications.

edges.label: Diamond data
edges.description: Import scripts fetch diamond pricing and availability from the Nivoda marketplace.

steps.note: Customer finds a ring and configures metal, size and stone
Cart and checkout requests save items and create a payment
Order is marked paid and confirmation email is sent
Customer fills in the bespoke wizard with their dream ring details
Enquiry is submitted to the server
Lead is saved and staff are emailed
Staff review and respond from the admin dashboard
Dashboard fetches order, inventory and sales data
Business logic processes the request against the database

tour.title: The shop
tour.note: This is the website customers see: a luxury jewellery storefront with product pages, filtering, a configurator for ring options and a shopping cart.

tour.title: Choosing a ring
tour.note: Each product page lets you pick metal, stone and size, view photos from every angle, and see the price update live.

tour.title: Behind the screens
tour.note: Every action — adding to cart, checking out, signing in — sends a request here. These are the Next.js API routes.

tour.title: Shared logic
tour.note: Business rules, database access, payment processing and email sending all live here so both the screens and the server can use them.

tour.title: Taking payments
tour.note: Stripe handles card payments. When a payment goes through, Stripe sends an alert back so the order updates automatically.

tour.title: Where the data lives
tour.note: PostgreSQL stores everything: customer accounts, orders, cart items, inventory levels and enquiries.

tour.title: Staff dashboard
tour.note: Staff sign in to a separate admin area to manage orders, update stock and reply to bespoke enquiries.

tour.title: Behind-the-scenes scripts
tour.note: Import scripts bring in products from the TMC supplier, build image sets and seed the database.
